## How to reproduce this file

1. Open `translation.ipynb` in this folder and run all cells. It saves
   `output/python-summary.csv` and `output/python-counts.csv`.
2. Render this file from the repository root:
   `quarto render assignments/assignment04-polyglot/submission/polyglot-parity.qmd`
3. Rendering builds the parity table from both languages and writes
   `parity-table.csv` into this folder.

All paths below are relative to the repository root, because `_quarto.yml`
sets `execute-dir: project`.

## Setup

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(tidyverse)
```

## Load and inspect

```{r}
nhanes <- read_csv("examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv",
                   show_col_types = FALSE)

dim(nhanes)
names(nhanes)
colSums(is.na(nhanes[, c("BMI", "IncomeGroup", "Gender")]))
```

## Part A: R summary of BMI by income group and gender

A descriptive, **unweighted** summary. Rows missing BMI, income group, or gender
are removed, and the number removed is reported rather than dropped silently.

```{r}
analysis <- nhanes |>
  filter(!is.na(BMI), !is.na(IncomeGroup), !is.na(Gender))

tibble(
  raw_rows      = nrow(nhanes),
  filtered_rows = nrow(analysis),
  dropped_rows  = nrow(nhanes) - nrow(analysis)
)

r_summary <- analysis |>
  group_by(IncomeGroup, Gender) |>
  summarise(
    n        = n(),
    mean_bmi = round(mean(BMI), 2),
    sd_bmi   = round(sd(BMI), 2),
    .groups  = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(IncomeGroup, Gender)

r_summary
```

## Part B: The same logic as a reusable function

The double curly braces ("curly-curly") around each argument let the function
take bare column names, the same way `filter()` and `group_by()` do.

```{r}
summarise_mean_sd <- function(data, value, group1, group2, digits = 2) {
  data |>
    filter(!is.na({{ value }}), !is.na({{ group1 }}), !is.na({{ group2 }})) |>
    group_by({{ group1 }}, {{ group2 }}) |>
    summarise(
      n          = n(),
      mean_value = round(mean({{ value }}), digits),
      sd_value   = round(sd({{ value }}), digits),
      .groups    = "drop"
    ) |>
    arrange({{ group1 }}, {{ group2 }})
}

r_function_summary <- summarise_mean_sd(nhanes, BMI, IncomeGroup, Gender)
r_function_summary

# Check: the function must reproduce Part A exactly
all.equal(
  r_function_summary |> rename(mean_bmi = mean_value, sd_bmi = sd_value),
  r_summary
)
```

### Reusing the function

**Swap the value column (Waist).** Same six income-by-gender groups, but fewer
rows, because Waist has more missing values than BMI.

```{r}
waist_summary <- summarise_mean_sd(nhanes, Waist, IncomeGroup, Gender)
waist_summary

identical(select(waist_summary, IncomeGroup, Gender),
          select(r_summary, IncomeGroup, Gender))
sum(waist_summary$n) - sum(r_summary$n)
```

**Swap a grouping column (Race).** Five race categories times two genders gives
ten grouped rows.

```{r}
race_summary <- summarise_mean_sd(nhanes, BMI, Race, Gender)
nrow(race_summary)
race_summary
```

## Part C: Parity check against Python

The Python translation is in `translation.ipynb` and uses `helpers.py`.

```{r}
py_dir <- "assignments/assignment04-polyglot/submission/output"
if (!file.exists(file.path(py_dir, "python-summary.csv"))) {
  stop("Run translation.ipynb first: output/python-summary.csv is missing.")
}

py_summary <- read_csv(file.path(py_dir, "python-summary.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
py_counts  <- read_csv(file.path(py_dir, "python-counts.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
py_value   <- function(metric) py_counts$python_value[py_counts$metric == metric]
```

### Group-by-group comparison

Rows are joined on the two grouping labels. `full_join()` keeps a group that
appears in only one language, so a label mismatch would show up as `NA`.

```{r}
group_check <- full_join(
  r_summary,
  py_summary,
  by = c("IncomeGroup", "Gender"),
  suffix = c("_r", "_py")
) |>
  mutate(
    n_match    = n_r == n_py,
    mean_match = abs(mean_bmi_r - mean_bmi_py) < 1e-9,
    sd_match   = abs(sd_bmi_r - sd_bmi_py) < 1e-9
  )

group_check |>
  select(IncomeGroup, Gender, n_r, n_py, mean_bmi_r, mean_bmi_py,
         sd_bmi_r, sd_bmi_py, n_match, mean_match, sd_match) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

### Parity table

```{r}
labels_r  <- paste(r_summary$IncomeGroup, r_summary$Gender, sep = " / ")
labels_py <- paste(py_summary$IncomeGroup, py_summary$Gender, sep = " / ")
values_ok <- all(group_check$n_match, group_check$mean_match, group_check$sd_match)

parity_table <- tibble(
  metric = c("raw_row_count", "raw_column_count", "filtered_row_count",
             "number_of_groups", "grouping_labels", "rounded_summary_values"),
  r_value = c(nrow(nhanes), ncol(nhanes), nrow(analysis), nrow(r_summary),
              paste(labels_r, collapse = "; "),
              paste(sprintf("%d, %.2f, %.2f", r_summary$n, r_summary$mean_bmi, r_summary$sd_bmi),
                    collapse = "; ")),
  python_value = c(py_value("raw_row_count"), py_value("raw_column_count"),
                   py_value("filtered_row_count"), nrow(py_summary),
                   paste(labels_py, collapse = "; "),
                   paste(sprintf("%d, %.2f, %.2f", py_summary$n, py_summary$mean_bmi, py_summary$sd_bmi),
                         collapse = "; "))
) |>
  mutate(
    match = r_value == python_value,
    match = if_else(metric == "rounded_summary_values", match & values_ok, match),
    notes = c(
      "Same CSV read by readr::read_csv and pandas.read_csv",
      "Same 18 variables",
      "R filter(!is.na(...)) vs pandas dropna(subset=[...]) on BMI, IncomeGroup, Gender",
      "group_by + summarise vs groupby + agg",
      "Same labels in the same order (arrange vs sort_values)",
      "n, mean, SD per group in label order (2 dp); also checked numerically in group_check; SD uses n - 1 in both"
    )
  ) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), as.character))

write_csv(parity_table, "assignments/assignment04-polyglot/submission/parity-table.csv")
knitr::kable(parity_table)
```

## Parity discussion

All `r sum(parity_table$match == "TRUE")` of `r nrow(parity_table)` parity checks
match: both languages start from `r nrow(nhanes)` rows, keep
`r nrow(analysis)` rows after removing missing BMI, income group, or gender, and
return the same `r nrow(r_summary)` groups with identical counts, means, and SDs
to two decimals. Two translation traps were checked rather than assumed: pandas
`std()` and R `sd()` both divide by n - 1, and `pandas.read_csv` needed
`low_memory = False` to stop it guessing mixed types for the sparse `Marital`
column (which does not affect this summary).

**Limitations.** These are unweighted sample statistics that include all ages,
so they describe the NHANES sample, not the U.S. population, and they do not
show that income causes any difference in BMI.
